verdict.summary: KLA is the highest-quality way in this batch to own rising semiconductor process complexity, but the equity is not automatically attractive at any price. Fiscal Q4 2026 revenue reached $3.66 billion, up 15.2% year over year, with 61.3% trailing gross margin and 42.5% operating margin; first-quarter fiscal 2027 guidance of $4.0 billion plus or minus $200 million implies continued momentum. The transmission is unusually direct: more process steps, tighter tolerances, advanced packaging and HBM raise inspection and metrology intensity even when wafer starts grow more slowly. Semiconductor Process Control supplied $3.26 billion of the latest quarter's $3.66 billion revenue, confirming that this is not a diffuse AI proxy. The counterweight is valuation at 39.5x EV/EBITDA and a chart below the 20-day and 50-day EMAs. The 74/100 fundamental score is defensible for margins, cash generation and installed-base service, but it does not activate a trade. With no captured regular-session opening bar, the displayed geometry remains dormant rather than actionable.

business.overview:
KLA sells inspection, metrology and process-control systems used by logic, foundry, memory and advanced-packaging manufacturers, then earns service revenue from the installed base. Semiconductor Process Control generated $3.257B of Q4 FY2026 revenue, while Specialty Semiconductor Process and PCB/Component Inspection contributed $160M and $241M.

The AI transmission channel is process intensity rather than GPU unit volume alone. Leading-edge logic, HBM and advanced packaging add layers, interconnects and yield-sensitive steps; each additional defect opportunity raises the economic value of inspection and metrology before a wafer or package can ship.

The model breaks if customers defer fab-equipment purchases, export controls remove accessible China demand, or competing process-control techniques reduce KLA content per wafer. Service cushions volatility, but customer procurement schedules, order pushouts and a premium valuation can still make earnings and the share price cyclical. Recurring service revenue reached $3.126B in FY2026, moderating but not eliminating wafer-fab-equipment cyclicality. The operating test is whether inspection intensity continues rising faster than wafer starts while export restrictions leave the company able to serve installed tools and collect cash.
business.moat: KLA's moat is the combination of defect-detection physics, proprietary optical/e-beam architectures, process libraries and the feedback data accumulated across a large installed base. Customers qualify these tools inside yield-control loops, so switching risks lost learning time and expensive yield excursions; the moat is strongest in Semiconductor Process Control, not uniformly across every segment.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: KLA had approximately 1.31B split-adjusted shares outstanding in the captured snapshot. FY2026 repurchases were $2.29B and dividends were $1.06B, while the June 2026 ten-for-one split changed units but created no economic dilution. The reviewed 10-Q, 10-K and dividend 8-K contain no prospectus supplement or ATM evidence; no equity issuance is inferred. Cash of $4.90B versus debt of $6.15B makes capital returns dependent on continued high free-cash-flow conversion, not on a net-cash balance sheet. KLA does not provide a current fully diluted point-in-time bridge in the reviewed materials, so no award estimate is added to the 1.31B split-adjusted basic count.

filingsReview.summary: 3 decision-relevant primary filing(s) are displayed with accession-specific findings. Grade B+ measures fundamentals; trade state wait measures timing and is evaluated separately.

filings.finding: The FY2026 Form 10-K supports $13.579B annual revenue, 61.3% GAAP gross margin, $3.126B service revenue and the three-segment mix; it also identifies China restrictions, customer capex timing and order pushouts as operating risks.
The August 6 Form 8-K reports a regular cash dividend decision; it does not register, offer or sell common stock and therefore provides no evidence of an ATM or primary equity issuance.

The March-quarter Form 10-Q reports nine-month revenue, cash generation, debt and segment results through March 31, 2026; it supplies the interim liquidity and process-control concentration bridge into the audited FY2026 Form 10-K.

macro.impact: KLA sits one capital-spending layer upstream from NVIDIA: the $108B NVIDIA Q3 revenue guide matters only insofar as foundries, memory makers and advanced packagers convert AI demand into more process steps and tighter yield budgets.
